newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down on lack of incentives.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down on lack of incentives.

text.p: Thai stocks closed down slightly in thin trade as locals sold stocks in most sectors amid a lack of fresh incentives and many foreigners were absent and away for the holidays, brokers said.
The SET index moved in a narrow range throughout the session and closed 3.60 points lower to 885.86 on 3.2 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dipped 0.23 point to 67.26.

"There was no fresh news to boost market investment today. Investors also found the government's key policy statement in parliament uninteresting," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.
Brokers said investors felt that the policy statement given by the new Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh was rather vague and it was quite similar to statements issued by previous governments.
The opposition and economic analysts said they wanted details.
"Foreign investors who play a significant role in the market during the past few months have left the market for the Christmas Christmas and New Year holidays," Somchai said.

Most of the key sectors on the board declined today. The banking sector fell most, dipping 1.01 percent, followed by the finance sector, which declined 0.94 percent. The communication sector slipped 0.56 percent.
Dhana Siam Finance and Securities topped the active list, rising 0.50 baht to 68.50. Thai Farmers Bank fell three to 131 while TelecomAsia declined 0.50 to 54 and Siam Cement slipped four to 812.
Support is seen by some brokers at 865 and resistance at 890 on Thursday.
